questions.prompt: What do you call the person who lives in the house next to yours?
questions.explanation: The person who lives next to you is your neighbour, whatever work that person does. A builder builds houses, a carpenter works with wood, and a gardener looks after plants and flowers, so all three name a job and not a place of living.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: "My grandmother works with her flowers all day. She is a ___ ."
questions.explanation: The verb garden gives the person who does it: garden + er = a gardener, and flowers are exactly what a gardener works with. A farmer grows crops in the fields, a cleaner cleans rooms and offices, and a player plays a game.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: "The pupils tidy ___ desks before they go home."
questions.explanation: The owners are the pupils, several people, that is they, so the possessive adjective is their. The word "his" names one boy, "her" names one girl, and "its" is for a thing or an animal.

questions.prompt: Sarra smiles from morning to evening, more than anybody else in her class. Complete: "Sarra is ___ girl in the class."
questions.explanation: The adjective happy ends in -y, so the y becomes i before the ending: the happiest. The form "the happier" compares two girls only, "the happyest" keeps the y that the rule changes, and "happiest" forgets the word the.

questions.prompt: A sign at the zoo tells the visitors not to give food to the animals. Which sentence is on the sign?

options.text: Don't giving food to the animals.
Not give food to the animals.
You don't give food to the animals.
Don't give food to the animals.

questions.explanation: A sign forbids, and a prohibition is Don't plus the bare verb: Don't give food to the animals. After Don't the verb never takes -ing, starting with "Not" copies the negative word of another language, and "You don't give" is a statement about what you do, not an order to everybody who reads the sign.

questions.prompt: In which of these words is the letter h NOT heard at all?
questions.explanation: The word hour begins like the word our: the h is written but no air is pushed out, so the sound is not there. In help, in home and in homework the h opens the word and you hear it clearly every time.
